segments.text: This paper follows two compact summaries of galaxy growth, the star-forming main sequence
and the mass-metallicity relation.
It measures how far JWST galaxies sit from a uniform local SDSS anchor.
The local baseline uses about 490,000 SDSS galaxies.
The high redshift side combines 180 NIR spec galaxies with 3,743 mire and sewer sources.
At fixed mass, star formation is elevated by 0.77 decks near Redshift 3.5 and reaches 1.94
decks beyond Redshift 6.
It is roughly 6 to almost 100 times the local rate.
On a matched directase scale, the metallicity deficits are minus 0.43, minus 0.37, and
minus 0.40 decks near Redshift 4.6, 5.3, and 7.2.
They do not deepen strongly.
The default tromontae anchor sits about 0.24 decks higher.
Recomputing 200,000 SDSS galaxies on the Tangred PP0403N2 scale prevents the high redshift
deficit from being overstated by about 0.1 decks.
JWST selection favors strong emission lines and high specific star formation.
The local relations are extrapolated at low mass.
This autonomous draft has no human clearance.
It is descriptive not validated.

This paper asks a narrower question, does the observed abundance exceed illustrious TNG

segments.text: This review asks why two surveys can report different galaxy metallicities before the galaxies themselves differ.
It separates three effects that are often mixed together, calibration scale, aperture, and diffuse ionized gas.
Theoretical photoionization calibrations and empirical electron temperature calibrations can differ by roughly 0.7 decks in absolute oxygen abundance.
That is about a factor of five before any physical evolution is inferred.
Below about 20% covering fraction, a fixed fiber can bias metallicity by more than 0.15 decks.
Central regions are typically richer, so the aperture can manufacture mass trends and even a false turnover.
Diffuse ionized gas can supply 30 to 60% of H alpha emission.
It's harder spectrum boosts low ionization line ratios, which can flatten or even invert the metallicity gradients inferred from integrated light.
Use one declared abundance scale with published conversions.
Enforce covering fraction floors or calibrated aperture corrections.
Then use integral field spectroscopy as the independent ground truth for the integrated relation.
The contribution is this framework, not a new metallicity measurement.
The thresholds come from published literature.
Automated review cleared status is a workflow gate, not human or journal peer review.
The draft is not validated.

segments.text: Illustra's TNG is calibrated to selected local observations.
This paper tests it away from that tuning point.
The key move is to subtract TNG's own local residual before comparing its evolution with SDSS and JWST.
At Redshift 0, TNG's star-forming main sequence sits 0.30 decks below SDSS,
while its mass-metallicity relation sits 0.12 decks above.
Those offsets are systematic starting errors, not high-redshift evolution.
After removing the starting error, TNG's internal main sequence growth is plus 1.30, 1.45,
and 1.61 decks at Redshift's 4, 5, and 6.
Observations rise only about 0.9 to 1.0 decks.
On one electron temperature anchored scale, observations evolved by about minus 0.40 decks in TNG
by about minus 0.27.
The remaining 0.13 decks gap lies within the residual calibration systematic.
The reproducible mismatch is the overstrong growth of star formation.
The chemical evolution comparison is not significant after scale matching.
Reproducing local observables neither validates the simulation,
nor makes every later disagreement physical.
Three data sets still require imperfect abundance scale reconciliation,
and the draft has no human clearance.
This is an autonomous descriptive result, not a validated measurement.
Automated review is not journal or human peer review.
